caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: The plot titled “AGNews, dirty-label, poison_num: 13” illustrates attack success rate (ASR) across a set of trigger words on the horizontal axis, with three series (“start,” “random,” and “end”) shown as colored lines with markers. The x-axis is categorical (no numeric scale) and lists trigger words in order: cf, bb, WNBA, ESPN, NHL, FIFA, Estadio, and athletics. The y-axis is labeled “ASR,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from 0.5 up to just under 1.0, with visible tick labels at regular 0.1 intervals (e.g., 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9). The “start” series is a green solid line with small circular markers, beginning near 0.76 at cf, dipping to about 0.72 at bb, rising to around 0.91 at WNBA, dropping to about 0.73 at ESPN, then increasing and staying high through NHL (~0.87) and FIFA (~0.88), reaching about 0.91 at Estadio, and ending near 0.84 at athletics. The “random” series is an orange solid line with x-shaped markers, starting near 0.50 at cf, increasing to about 0.54 at bb, peaking around 0.93 at WNBA, dropping to roughly 0.63 at ESPN, rising to about 0.75 at NHL, dipping to around 0.70 at FIFA, increasing to about 0.83 at Estadio, and ending near 0.78 at athletics. The “end” series is a purple solid line with circular markers, starting near 0.62 at cf, dipping to about 0.58 at bb, rising to its highest point around 0.95 at WNBA, dropping to about 0.73 at ESPN, moving to roughly 0.81 at NHL and about 0.79 at FIFA, increasing to around 0.90 at Estadio, and ending near 0.82 at athletics.
